timeline: 2024-11-10 - Intro call (CTO + Head of Search). KPIs: 50M docs, p50 latency <60ms, cost/query <$0.01

notes:
Top-level: CTO worried about subtle quality regressions when moving embeddings -> new open model. Wants rigorous evals and rollback gates.
POC specifics: indexing scale target 50M docs, current POC uses 600k sample; QPS expected 200-300 steady, peak bursts 800.
Latency/Cost targets: p50 <60ms total (search + lightweight rerank), p95 <250ms for user-facing flows; cost per query target <$0.01 averaged over mixed workloads.
Models: currently using SBERT-like embeddings + BERT cross-encoder reranker. Migration candidate = open-embed-v2 + distilled cross-encoder for rerank. Concern: distilled reranker cuts latency but may miss rare legal precedents.
Evals: team requires Redwood-driven eval harness (MRR, NDCG@10, recall@100, explicit failure categories) and automated regression alerts tied to prompt/test-suite.
Rollout plan: start 5% canary -> evaluate over 72h on production traffic + offline holdout; A/B buckets should be user-consistent (sticky) to capture downstream UX metrics.
Quote from CTO: "If we lose edge cases in legal precedence search we risk product trust. Don’t flip without strong eval gates."
Operational: wants VPC/private deployment with KMS and 7-year audit logging retention. Needs SLA for failover to hosted variants during upgrades.
Support artifacts: pricing sensitivity; prefer committed Dedicated pool but needs ability to autoscale bursts.
Open asks for Redwood: 1) run Eval suite and share concrete per-query failure examples, 2) propose canary policy + rollout automation, 3) cost modeling for estimated 50M index with hybrid rerank
